# The off-socket Neural Link adapter fails six window specs

## Context

#20451 retires the Brain-gated e2e tier. Every Neural Link spec now runs off-socket in the engine tier, or `LOCAL_ONLY` in `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` states why it stays local (PR #20584). On 2026-11-08 a local off-socket probe ran the 42 window-driving specs: 37 files were clean, and they move into the tier. Six window specs fail on the adapter and pass over the Bridge. With the Brain tier gone, no CI job runs them. This ticket owns their `LOCAL_ONLY` entry.

## The Problem

Measured off-socket, locally, on one worker:

- **Re-boot.**
  - `workstation/DockSplitterZoneIdNL` "3 consecutive boots" fails 3/3 off-socket and passes 2/2 over the Bridge (#20461). After a re-boot the dock host never becomes visible: the adapter's SharedWorker handle does not survive the re-boot.
  - `workstation/WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL` (2 arms) and `workstation/WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` (4 arms) fail after `page.reload` with `neuralLink.connectToApp(...)`: "the page's App Worker … did not initialize Neo.ai.Client within 30000 ms".
  - `workstation/WorkstationFiveBeatNL` (2 arms) times out in its `boot()`, which waits 30 s for `.workstation-tour-play` after re-navigating.
- **Closed bound page.** `realworld/EmailMultiWindowNL` closes its source page (`page.close({runBeforeUnload: true})`). Then: "Tearing down "neuralLink" exceeded the test timeout of 90000ms".
- **Topology.** `neural-link/WindowOps` compares a drag receipt with `popupWindow.innerRect.x` from `get_window_topology`. The value is `undefined`: a `toBeCloseTo` matcher error at line 158.

**Measured at intake (2026-11-08), each cause now established:**

- **Re-boot** (`DockSplitterZoneIdNL`, `WorkstationFiveBeatNL`): the adapter's held CDP session keeps the App SharedWorker alive past its last client. The re-booted page connects to that survivor (same `targetId`), whose Data, VDom and Canvas siblings started fresh, and never finishes booting. A four-arm probe settled it: holding the session, releasing only the writer pair, and attaching without a call all fail, while detaching before the navigation passes.
- **Closed bound page** (`EmailMultiWindowNL`): the hang follows the context's *last* window closing. The held App Worker then never answers and emits no target event.
- **Topology** (`WindowOps`): `Neo.util.Rectangle` is a `DOMRect`, and CDP `returnByValue` drops its accessor `x`/`y`, while the Bridge's JSON wire keeps them. The spec then also needs the Bridge's refusal of an unknown window (`resolveWindowTarget`).
- **Not a reload** (`WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL`, `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL`): they cold-boot a second browser context and bind it by worker id, which the adapter cannot reach. They keep `LOCAL_ONLY` under #20614.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.mjs` is the adapter. Its `get_window_topology` reads `Neo.manager.Window.items` in the App Worker, then adds the windows of `Neo.apps` that have no item, and those come without `innerRect`. An item gets `innerRect` only from `Neo.manager.Window#onWindowConnect` (`src/manager/Window.mjs:181`), and only when the connect carried `windowData`.
- `test/playwright/sharedWorkerAppWorker.mjs` (`attachPageSharedAppWorker`) holds the page's SharedWorker handle, the one a re-boot invalidates.
- `test/playwright/externalBrainSelection.mjs` lists the eligible specs (`ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS`). `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` holds `RUN_PATHS`, `LOCAL_ONLY` and the duration table the shards balance by.

## The Fix

In the adapter:

1. After a re-boot (reload or re-navigation), re-attach to the page's App Worker instead of keeping the first handle.
2. Release a binding whose page closed, instead of waiting on it at teardown.
3. Find why the `WindowOps` popup reaches the topology without `innerRect`, and make the off-socket topology carry it.

Then, for each spec green on a hosted run:

- move it from `LOCAL_ONLY` into `ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS`, and into `RUN_PATHS` for `workstation/`;
- give it a duration in `e2eEngineDurations.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DockSplitterZoneIdNL` "3 consecutive boots" passes off-socket 3/3 locally, red first: 0/3 on the base.
- [ ] Each of the six specs passes off-socket on two hosted engine-tier runs and leaves `LOCAL_ONLY`. A spec that cannot keeps an entry that states its measured cause.
- [ ] Each adapter change has an arm that fails without it.

## Out of Scope

- The Bridge and Brain-service classes of `LOCAL_ONLY`. They test the Brain itself and stay local.
- Rewriting Brain-service specs to the off-socket SDK.

* test(e2e): FilmTour leaves the hosted tier; the shards balance by measured time (#20451)

The 14-shard run at 70b1e0e put FilmTour on a shard of its own. Its
viewer-driven arm's grid throw carried no momentum once: 474 px of the 960
its witness requires. The rerun carried it, and so did the other three throws
(1051–1133 px). A required context cannot hold an arm that flakes one run in
two. FilmTour still runs off-socket, so it stays adapter-eligible for local
runs, but it leaves RUN_PATHS for an observed exclusion owned by #20593.

populations() counts a declared exclusion only once. The GPU class was every
Brain-free workstation file that RUN_PATHS does not name, so an exclusion in
workstation/ was subtracted twice.

e2eEngineDurations.json is rebuilt from that run's log with
--engine-durations: all 186 files measured, with no Brain-tier seed and no
median fallback left. The tier stays on 14 shards. The run's slowest shard
took 3.7 min of the 5-minute step, about 45 s more than its summed file
times, and fewer shards would push the busiest step past 4 minutes."

* fix(test): the off-socket adapter releases a held SharedWorker session before its page re-boots (#20587)

A CDP session attached to the App SharedWorker keeps it alive past its last
client. A page that re-booted while the adapter held it connected to that
survivor, whose Data, VDom and Canvas siblings had started fresh, and never
finished booting (a four-arm probe: holding the session fails, detaching before
the navigation passes, the writer pair is irrelevant). A worker kept alive after
its last window closed never answers again either, which hung the fixture's
teardown.

- dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink: a document request of the bound page waits until the
  session is released; the next call attaches the App Worker the new document
  started; the context's last window closing releases it too. `appWorker` holds
  dedicated workers only.
- sharedWorkerAppWorker: a closed handle rejects every later call at once.
- get_window_topology hands rects over as the wire's JSON (Neo.util.Rectangle is
  a DOMRect, whose x / y CDP's returnByValue drops), and a window operation on a
  window the topology does not hold is refused before the App Worker sees it, as
  the Bridge's resolveWindowTarget refuses it.

DockSplitterZoneIdNL, WorkstationFiveBeatNL, EmailMultiWindowNL and WindowOps
pass off-socket and join the engine tier. WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL and
WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL bind a second browser context by worker id, which the
adapter cannot reach; they stay LOCAL_ONLY under #20614.
